summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, chronic systolic heart failure, seizure disorder, and esophageal reflux was admitted from transplant clinic with a one-day history of fever, myalgias, dizziness, and diarrhea. Initial evaluation revealed a low-grade fever and stable vital signs after IV fluids. Chest X-ray showed clear lungs and no free air, and EKG was unchanged. Rapid flu testing was negative, and blood cultures showed no growth. His symptoms were attributed to a mild viral upper respiratory infection. He received supportive care, including hydration and antipyretics, and completed his scheduled hemodialysis. He improved rapidly, afebrile by the morning of discharge, and was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue his home medications and follow up with his specialists.
